1 Solution Summary

This manual is designed to guide Lenders through the use of the Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery
Technology (SMART) System.

1.1 Features

The Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery Technology (SMART) System is comprised of individual
modules designed to assist the user in searching for specific loan information and performing related
functions. The modules currently available include the following:

Loan Module: Query and review loan information at a detailed level, add new loan records to
the system, and edit existing loan information.

Servicing Module: Assign mortgage servicing templates to individual loans, track the status of
each servicing template, and generate the corresponding servicing forms and letters.
Bankruptcy Module: Maintain, track, and edit bankruptcy information for individual loan
records.

Foreclosure Module: Manage loan records in the foreclosure process. Module provides a
timeline of the required foreclosure steps and tracks the scheduled foreclosure activity vs. the
completed foreclosure activity.

Mortgage Release Module: Initiate the loan release process for satisfied loans, track the release
status, and generate the corresponding release forms and letters.

Cash Management Module: Track and manage incoming payments from Pay.Gov, submit
disbursement checks, search for transactions and review the TROR and Trial Balance reports.
Customer Service Module: Create, view, and manage tickets. Create and edit call logs and ticket
actions.

Maintenance Module: Manage user account, reset user passwords, and update ticket round
robin.

2.4.1. My Dashboard

The default page you come to after you have logged into SMART is the [My DASHBOARD] page. Under the
tab [My DASHBOARD] you have seven options: My Loans, My Tickets, LSC Inbox, Supervisor Inbox, HUD
Inbox, Action List, and Unassigned Tickets.

2.4.2 Loanand Mail

The [LOAN] tab directs the user to the Loan Module in SMART. Here you have three options: Search,
Loan Wizard, and PMC Queue. Under [MAIL] you have two options: NCF Queue and Document Wizard.

2.4.3 Servicing

The [SERVICING] tab directs the user to the Servicing Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.4 Bankruptcy

The [BANKRUPTCY] tab directs the user to the Bankruptcy Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.5 Foreclosure
The [FORECLOSURE] tab directs the user to the Foreclosure Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.6 Mortgage Release
The [MORTGAGE RELEASE] tab directs the user to the Mortgage Release Module. Here you have four
options: Mortgage Search, Check Search, Print Batch Checks, and Print Rejects Checks.

2.4.7. Cash Management
Under [CASH MANAGEMENT] you have seven options: Trial Balance, TROR Report, Transaction Search, SPS,
Pay.Gov Dashboard, Pay.Gov Queue, and Review Failed CSV.

2.4.8 Customer Service
The [CUSTOMER SERVICE] tab directs the user to the Customer Service Module. Here you have three
options: Ticket Search, Create New Ticket, and CRM Review Queue.

2.4.9 Reports

Under [REPORTS] you have four options: Customer Service, Director Reports, Servicing/Release Reports,
and Accounting Reports.

2.4.10 User Information and Roles

Select your user name to view and update your personal identification and contact information. You
may also change your password and security questions. From the [ROLE] drop-down menu, select the
role in which to view the SMART System.

The user is required to change their password every 30 days. The system maintains a password history,

If the user logs into SMART after their password is expired between 30 days and 90 days from their last
password change, they will be redirected to change their password. If the user has not logged on for 90
days, their account will be disabled. In order to reactivate their account, they will need to contact the
Help Desk. For information on how to contact the Help Desk, see Section 14: Getting Help.

3.4.1 Change Disposition
For CRM and SMART Customer Service Tickets, the disposition for a ticket can be changed through the
[CHANGE DisposiTION] link from the Action column.

Step1: Inside the Supervisor Inbox, click on the [CHANGE Disposition] link from the Actions
column.

Figure 22: Change Disposition (Edit Mode)

Step 2: Select a new disposition from the Disposition dropdown menu. Options in Table 1.
Step 3: = Click [SAVE].
Step 4: From the confirmation pop-up, click [SUBMIT].

The disposition column will update to display the new edit. Changing the disposition from the
Supervisor Inbox will enter the ticket into the respective round robin queen and assign to a new agent
from the respective round robin queue. The ticket can only enter the round robin queue through the
Supervisor Inbox. The new designee will receive an email.

Search Field Definition

FHA Case # FHA Case number for each loan

Loan Skey SMART system identification number unique to each loan

Loan # HUD identification number for each loan.

Last 4 Digits of SSN The last four digits of the Borrower’s Social Security Number
Close Box # Physical location of stored files

Note Text Searches any word within the content of notes within the Notes tab of the Loan Record
Current Servicer Servicer/Lender associated with the FHA Case

Exception Type Type of Exception filed in the Exceptions tab

Result Headers Search criteria columns to be displayed in the Search Results table
Loan Program Type of program associated with the loan

Label Printed Indicator of whether or not a hard copy file has been generated for the loan
Loan Status Current high-level status of the Loan (Open or Closed)

Loan State Detailed Status of the loan

Payment Plan Type of Payment Plan associated with the loan

Note Type Type of note within the Notes tab of the Loan Record

Borrower Name Name of the Borrower

Property Address Address of the loan property

Property City City wherein the loan property is located

Property State State wherein the loan property is located

Property Zip Code Zip Code wherein the loan property is located

Note Created By SMART User who created Notes in the Notes tab

Claim Servicer Servicer/Lender associated with a Claim

Loan Create Date Date that a loan was entered into the SMART system

Loan Close Date Date that a loan was closed

File Rec’d Date The File Received Date of a loan

EHLP Project # EHLP Project Number

Keyword Searches any word within the Search Results data table

Note Create Date Date that the Note in the Notes tab was created

Payee/Holder of Record Servicer/Lender assigned as a Holder of Record

4.4 Accessing Detailed Loan Information

Opening a Loan Record from the search results will navigate the user to the Loan Record page. The Loan
Record page consists of multiple tabs that provide detailed Loan information.

Step1: Click [LOAN] from the top Navigation menu. Select [SEARCH] from the dropdown.

Step 2: In the Loan Search Screen, select the Loan Program from the Loan Program drop down.

Step 3: Click [START SEARCH]. 50 records will display in the Search Results Dashboard.

Step 4: From the Search Results Dashboard, click on either the Loan Skey, FHA Case #, and Loan #
to open the loan.

Figure 60: Loan Record (example)

To minimize the loan record, click on the black arrow (+) located left of the Loan Record page title. To
maximize, re-click on the black arrow.

To minimize the Borrower & Property Information and Additional Loan Information, click on the white
arrow (Ez) located left of the of the Borrower & Property information box or the white arrow located left
of the Additional Loan Information. To maximize, re-click on the white arrow.

On each Loan Record page, the selection of tabs displayed is dynamic and varies depending on the Loan
program of the selected loan. The colors of the tabs show at a glance whether data exists in the tab or

not.

Note: Loans that are Closed are all Read Only.

4.4.3.7 View/Add/Edit Property Picture

If property pictures have been attached to a Loan, a camera icon will appear next to the property
record. Loan Property Pictures can be viewed in the Property Inspection tab where the Active Property
photo will be displayed.

Step 1: — Click on [EpIT ITEM] located in the Actions column of the Property Inspection dashboard to
navigate to Property Inspection (Edit Mode).

Step 2: Scroll to the bottom of the page to view the Property Picture dashboard.

Step 3: To adda picture, click on the [ADD PicTURE] button located under the Property Pictures
title. To edit a picture, click on [EDIT PictuRE] located in the Actions column of the
Property Pictures dashboard.

Step 4: Drag and drop a picture or click on the Upload button to upload a file (if you are using
Internet Explorer, you can only click to upload). (Note; Only TIF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, or PDF
files are accepted.)

Step 5: Complete all required fields and click [SAVE].

Step 6: On the Confirmation Pop-up, click [SUBMIT].

After saving, the user redirects to Property Inspection edit mode and if the user scrolls down the
Property Picture dashboard will display with new addition.

4.4.4.6 View/Add/Edit Property Picture

If property pictures have been attached to a Loan, a camera icon will appear next to the property
record. Loan Property Pictures can be viewed in the Property Inspection tab where the Active Property
photo will be displayed.

Step 1: — Click on [EpIT ITEM] located in the Actions column of the Property Inspection dashboard to
navigate to Property Inspection (Edit Mode).

Step 2: Scroll to the bottom of the page to view the Property Picture dashboard.

Step 3: To adda picture, click on [ADD PictuRE] located under the Property Pictures title. To edit a
picture, click on [EDIT PicTuRE] located in the Actions column of the Property Pictures
dashboard.

Step 4: Drag and drop a picture or click on the Upload button to upload a file (if you are using
Internet Explorer, you can only click to upload). (Note; Only TIF, JPG, JPEG, PNG, or PDF
files are accepted.)

Step 5: Complete all required fields and click [SAVE].

Step 6: On the Confirmation Pop-up, click [SUBMIT].

After saving, the user redirects to Property Inspection edit mode and if the user scrolls down the
Property Picture dashboard will display with new addition.

navigate to Property Inspection (Edit Mode).

dashboard.

files are accepted.)

4.5 Loan Transactions

45.1 Transactions

Transactions are any time there is a monetary impact on the financial statements of the business, or any
time there is a change to the balance of a loan. Transactions are available for all loan programs except
HECM-A, HECM-lI, and SF Data Request.

If the transaction reduces the Unpaid Principal Balance to SO then the following will occur:

1. Payoff Request Timeline in the Servicing Module will automatically open and close with all steps
marked as complete with today’s timestamp.

2. Mortgage Release Timeline in the Mortgage Release Module will automatically open with the
first step marked as complete with today’s timestamp.

3. The Loan will close after the user refreshes the page.

4, The amount in the Payoff Letter will update to reflect the new Total Payoff Amount found in the
Payoff Tab, which is SO.

5. Arecord will automatically insert into the Transaction Tab.

If the transaction reduces the Unpaid Principal Balance to SO and there is already an open Mortgage
Release Timeline, then the following will occur:
1. Payoff Request Timeline in the Servicing Module will automatically open and close with all steps
marked as complete with today’s timestamp.
2. The Loan will close after the user refreshes the page.
3. The amount in the Payoff Letter will update to reflect the new Total Payoff Amount found in the
Payoff Tab, which is SO.

SMART USER MANUAL | HUD.ADMIN | VERSION 1.43.0 | JUNE 2, 2020 | 91

4.5.1.1.3 CTB Transaction

The Transaction, CTB — Type 15 Termination Conveyance of Title for Benefits, is only available to be
entered into the system between the 1st and the 25" of the month. Once one CTB Transaction has
been entered, no other transaction may be entered except a RCTB — Reversal — Type 15 Termination
Conveyance of Title for Benefits.

Step 1: Click on [ADD TRANSACTION] button located under the Transactions title to navigate to the
Add Transaction window.

Loan Summary Loan Detal_Loan Filng Loan Recording BortowersPropertyinspection Documents Notes Mortpage Release Exceptions Servicing Foreclosure Bankruptcy Disbursements Payort (RECERENEEI customer service

RCTS - Reversal - Type 15 Termination Conveyance of Tite for Benefits

Figure 208: Add Transaction After CTB Transaction Submitted

Step 2: From the Transaction Type drop down menu, select CTB.

Step 3: The Transaction Amount will auto-fill to the Unpaid Principal Balance and is not editable.
Step 4: Complete all required fields and click [SAVE].

Step5: On the Confirmation Pop-up, click [SUBMIT].

If there is no prior CTB Transaction, the following occurs after saving:
1. The user redirects to the Transaction tab displaying the new transaction.
2. An auto-note is created in the Notes tab.
3. The loan is Closed.

If there is a prior CTB Transaction, the following occurs after saving:
1. The user redirects to the Transaction tab displaying the new transaction.
2. An auto-note is created in the Notes tab.
3. The loan is Re-Opened.

4.5.3. Payoff Request

When a mortgage has been satisfied, the user can initiate the release process and assign a predefined
template of release activity steps to the satisfied Loan Record. The release activity templates provide
the user with a list of required steps in a timeline format so that the user can schedule and track the
progress of the Mortgage Release Activity. Payoff Requests are available for the following Loan
Programs: Partial Claim, PMM, and EHLP.

4.5.3.1 Scenario 1: Received Request for Payoff
Step 1: — Click [SERVICING] from the top Navigation menu. Select [SEARCH] from the dropdown.
Step 2: Search for a Loan Record by selecting the search criteria and click [START SEARCH].
Step 3: From the Search Result Dashboard, click on either Loan Skey, FHA Case #, or Loan # to
open the Loan Record. You are automatically directed to the Servicing tab.

4.5.3.2 Scenario 2: Received Payoff Check Without Payoff Request

If the Payoff Check was received prior to entering a Payoff Request in the Servicing Module, the user can
enter the payoff directly through the Payoff tab. In the steps listed above, begin the process at Step 13.

If the Total Payoff Amount is now SO, then the following will occur:
1. Payoff Request Timeline will automatically open and close with all steps marked as complete
with today’s timestamp.
2. Mortgage Release Timeline will automatically open with the first step marked as complete with
today’s timestamp.
3. Arecord will automatically insert in the Transaction tab.
The Loan will close after the user refreshes the page.
5. The amount in the Payoff letter will update to reflect the new Total Payoff Amount found in the
Payoff Tab, which is $0.00.

5

If the Total Payoff Amount is SO and there is already an open Mortgage Release Timeline, then the
following will occur:

1. Payoff Request Timeline will automatically open and close with the last two steps marked as

complete with today’s timestamp.

2. Arecord will automatically insert in the Transaction tab.

3. The Loan will close after the user refreshes the page.
The amount in the Payoff Letter will update to reflect the new Total Payoff Amount found in the Payoff
Tab, which is $0.00.

9 Using the Cash Management Module

Within the Cash Management Module, there are two types of transactions: SMART and Pay.Gov.
SMART tickets are created using the SMART application. Pay.Gov transactions are payments that are
made on Pay.Gov and submitted via a validated submission forum to SMART. The © icon will appear
before or after the Pay.Gov Ticket Number anywhere a transaction appears (such as the Transactions
Tab within the Loan Module, Trial Balance - USSGL Account, and the Transaction Search Screen).

Data is refreshed on a nightly basis; however, if users need to refresh the data for today’s transactions,
they can do so from Cash Management. The Cash Management screens will display Transactions as of
the last data refresh.

@ Trial Balance

Figure 309: Data Refresh

Cc Last Data Refresh 12/04/2019 03-51-03 PM EST

Figure 310: Last Data Refresh

From any non-Pay.Gov screen under the Cash Management header, users will see a gold button below
the Help Desk button. By clicking it once, users can see the last time transaction data was refreshed. By
clicking it once more, users will refresh the data. Allow 1-2 minutes for the page to load.

Figure 322: SPS — Checks Submitted / Checks Status

Immediately after submitting a check for processing, the process is as follows:

Step1: Status is Pending Processing. The following actions are available:

e This action sends the check back to the Unprocessed Checks table.

e This action sends the DAT file and the SPS 440 file to Treasury. (See #2)

Step 2: If the action [SUBMIT SPS FILES] is selected, status is In Transit Expected Delivery
MM/DD/YY 9:00 PM EST. The following actions are available:

e [REQUEST CANCELLATION]: SMART will send the HelpDesk an email to remove the
files from the Treasury Server. (If this action is selected before 9:00 PM EST on
the same day, see #3. If the action was not taken by 9:00 PM EST on the same
day, see #5.)

Step 3: Status is Pending Cancellation. No actions are available. (If the HelpDesk successfully
removed the files from the Treasury Server see #4. If not, see #5).

Step 4: Status is Cancelled. No actions available. The check is reverted back to the Unprocessed
Checks table.

9.5 Pay.Gov Dashboard

To access the Pay.Gov Dashboard, click [CASH MANAGEMENT] from the top Navigation menu and then
select [PAY.GOv DASHBOARD] from the dropdown. The Pay.Gov Dashboard summarizes all settled
transactions submitted from Pay.Gov lender and non-lender forms regardless of where the transaction
is in the validation process. The Dashboard is organized by the daily .xml file that is retrieved from
Pay.Gov by the SMART system. Each file name contains a link that will open a detailed dashboard with
all transactions retrieved from that day.

that was submitted on Pay.Gov, make corrections, and then upload the corrected file to pass
through the CSV validation again.

10 Using the Customer Service Module

Within the Customer Service Module, there are two types of tickets: SMART and CRM. SMART tickets
are created using the SMART application. CRM (Customer Relationship Management), tickets are
created in a separate program used to track customer service tickets. CRM tickets are then imported
into SMART. The @ icon will appear before or after the CRM Ticket Number anywhere a Ticket appears
(such as My Tickets, All Inboxes, Ticket Search Screen, and within the Customer Service Module Ticket
Information Screen).

Additionally, there are two types of tickets: sys tickets and non-sys tickets. If a Loan No. exists for a
ticket, then that system is sys. If a Loan No. exists for a ticket, then that system is non-sys.

10.1 Ticket Search

Customer Service Tickets can be retrieved through various combinations of the search criteria available
on the Ticket Search Screen.

14.2 Solutions to Common Problems

Problems with SMART fall into three categories: internet issues, browser issues, and SMART issues.
Please follow the steps below to resolve each issue.

14.2.1 Internet and Browser Issues

The Primary characteristic of this issue is a delay when loading a page. At the conclusion of this long
delay, a message may display indicating there is a problem with internet access. Alternatively, pages
may seem to load but appear blank. If a page has not loaded or displayed after 30 seconds, please
follow the steps below.

Note: Not all steps have to be completed; start with Step 1 and keep working until the issue is resolved.
Once the issue is resolved, skip all remaining steps and return to your training session.

Step1: Refresh the page using the browser’s [REFRESH] button.

Step 2: If the issue still exists, close all browser windows, wait 10 seconds, then open a new
browser window and return to SMART.

SMART USER MANUAL | HUD.ADMIN | VERSION 1.43.0 | JUNE 2, 2020 | 178

Step 3:

Step 4:

@SMART

Check your internet connectivity — do other sites display without issue? If so, proceed to
Step 2. Otherwise, the issue may be that the browser is unable to connect to the internet.
Check all connections and try again. If the problem persists, contact your network
administrator or your Internet Service Provider.

Send email to he!pdesk@hudnsc.org. Include your email address, your contact
information, and a description of what happened leading up to and following the issue.

14.2.2. SMART Issues

SMART issues may be errors which display on-screen or situations where data may not be saved
properly. If you experience either of these problems, please contact Support via email.

Step 1:
Step 2:

Step 3:

Use [PRTSC] on the keyboard to capture an image of the screen.

Compose a new email message and paste ([CTRL+V} on the keyboard) the screen image
into the message. Be sure to include your Username, your contact information, a
description of what module or page you were viewing, and what you were doing (or trying
to do) at the time the error occurred.

Send the email to helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

14.3 Getting More Help

If you are experiencing technical difficulties, please contact the SMART support team via email at
helpdesk@hudnsc.org. For general questions and/or class availability concerns, please contact the
SMART administration team via email at helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

When emailing, pleases include as much information as possible relating to the problem, including print
screen(s) of the error.

@SMART

1 Solution Summary

This manual is designed to guide Lenders through the use of the Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery
Technology (SMART) System.

1.1 Features

The Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery Technology (SMART) System is comprised of individual
modules designed to assist the user in searching for specific loan information and performing related
functions. The modules currently available include the following:

Loan Module: Query and review loan information at a detailed level, add new loan records to
the system, and edit existing loan information.

Servicing Module: Assign mortgage servicing templates to individual loans, track the status of
each servicing template, and generate the corresponding servicing forms and letters.
Bankruptcy Module: Maintain, track, and edit bankruptcy information for individual loan
records.

Foreclosure Module: Manage loan records in the foreclosure process. Module provides a
timeline of the required foreclosure steps and tracks the scheduled foreclosure activity vs. the
completed foreclosure activity.

Mortgage Release Module: Initiate the loan release process for satisfied loans, track the release
status, and generate the corresponding release forms and letters.

Cash Management Module: Track and manage incoming payments from Pay.Gov, submit
disbursement checks, search for transactions and review the TROR and Trial Balance reports.
Customer Service Module: Create, view, and manage tickets. Create and edit call logs and ticket
actions.

Maintenance Module: Manage user account, reset user passwords, and update ticket round
robin.

Search Field Definition

FHA Case # FHA Case number for each loan

Loan Skey SMART system identification number unique to each loan

Loan # HUD identification number for each loan.

Last 4 Digits of SSN The last four digits of the Borrower’s Social Security Number

Close Box # Physical location of stored files

Note Text Searches any word within the content of notes within the Notes tab of the Loan Record
Current Servicer Servicer/Lender associated with the FHA Case

Exception Type Type of Exception filed in the Exceptions tab

Result Headers

Search criteria columns to be displayed in the Search Results table

Loan Program

Type of program associated with the loan

Label Printed

Indicator of whether or not a hard copy file has been generated for the loan

Loan Status

Current high-level status of the Loan (Open or Closed)

Loan State Detailed Status of the loan

Payment Plan Type of Payment Plan associated with the loan

Note Type Type of note within the Notes tab of the Loan Record
Borrower Name Name of the Borrower

Property Address Address of the loan property

Property City City wherein the loan property is located

Property State State wherein the loan property is located

Property Zip Code Zip Code wherein the loan property is located

Note Created By

SMART User who created Notes in the Notes tab

Claim Servicer

Servicer/Lender associated with a Claim

Loan Create Date

Date that a loan was entered into the SMART system

Loan Close Date

Date that a loan was closed

File Rec’d Date

The File Received Date of a loan

EHLP Project # EHLP Project Number

Keyword Searches any word within the Search Results data table
Note Create Date Date that the Note in the Notes tab was created
Payee/Holder of Record Servicer/Lender assigned as a Holder of Record

4.2 Accessing Detailed Loan Information

Opening a Loan Record from the search results will navigate the user to the Loan Record page. The Loan
Record page consists of multiple tabs that provide detailed Loan information.

Step1: Click [LOAN] from the top Navigation menu. Select [SEARCH] from the dropdown.

Step 2: In the Loan Search Screen, select the Loan Program from the Loan Program drop down.

Step 3: Click [START SEARCH]. 50 records will display in the Search Results Dashboard.

Step 4: From the Search Results Dashboard, click on either the Loan Skey, FHA Case #, and Loan #
to open the loan.

Figure 25: Loan Record (example)

To minimize the loan record, click on the black arrow (+) located left of the Loan Record page title. To
maximize, re-click on the black arrow.

To minimize the Borrower & Property Information and Additional Loan Information, click on the white
arrow (Ez) located left of the of the Borrower & Property information box or the white arrow located left
of the Additional Loan Information. To maximize, re-click on the white arrow.

On each Loan Record page, the selection of tabs displayed is dynamic and varies depending on the Loan
program of the selected loan. The colors of the tabs show at a glance whether data exists in the tab or

not.

Note: Loans that are Closed are all Read Only.

6 Using the Customer Service Module

Within the Customer Service Module, there are two types of tickets: SMART and CRM. SMART tickets
are created using the SMART application. CRM (Customer Relationship Management), tickets are
created in a separate program used to track customer service tickets. CRM tickets are then imported
into SMART. The @ icon will appear before or after the CRM Ticket Number anywhere a Ticket appears
(such as My Tickets, All Inboxes, Ticket Search Screen, and within the Customer Service Module Ticket
Information Screen).

Additionally, there are two types of tickets: sys tickets and non-sys tickets. If a Loan No. exists for a
ticket, then that system is sys. If a Loan No. exists for a ticket, then that system is non-sys.

6.1 Ticket Search

Customer Service Tickets can be retrieved through various combinations of the search criteria available
on the Ticket Search Screen.

8.2 Solutions to Common Problems

Problems with SMART fall into three categories: internet issues, browser issues, and SMART issues.
Please follow the steps below to resolve each issue.

8.2.1 Internet and Browser Issues

The Primary characteristic of this issue is a delay when loading a page. At the conclusion of this long
delay, a message may display indicating there is a problem with internet access. Alternatively, pages
may seem to load but appear blank. If a page has not loaded or displayed after 30 seconds, please
follow the steps below.

Note: Not all steps have to be completed; start with Step 1 and keep working until the issue is resolved.
Once the issue is resolved, skip all remaining steps and return to your training session.

Step1: Refresh the page using the browser’s [REFRESH] button.

Step 2: If the issue still exists, close all browser windows, wait 10 seconds, then open a new
browser window and return to SMART.

SMART USER MANUAL | HUD.CS | VERSION 1.43.0 | JUNE 2, 2020 | 76

@SMART

Step 3: Check your internet connectivity — do other sites display without issue? If so, proceed to
Step 2. Otherwise, the issue may be that the browser is unable to connect to the internet.
Check all connections and try again. If the problem persists, contact your network
administrator or your Internet Service Provider.

Step 4: Send email to helpdesk@hudnsc.org. Include your email address, your contact
information, and a description of what happened leading up to and following the issue.

8.2.2 SMART Issues

SMART issues may be errors which display on-screen or situations where data may not be saved
properly. If you experience either of these problems, please contact Support via email.

Step 1: Use [PRTSC] on the keyboard to capture an image of the screen.

Step 2: Compose a new email message and paste ([CTRL+V} on the keyboard) the screen image
into the message. Be sure to include your Username, your contact information, a
description of what module or page you were viewing, and what you were doing (or trying
to do) at the time the error occurred.

Step 3: Send the email to helopdesk@hudnsc.org.

8.3 Getting More Help

If you are experiencing technical difficulties, please contact the SMART support team via email at
helpdesk@hudnsc.org. For general questions and/or class availability concerns, please contact the
SMART administration team via email at helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

When emailing, pleases include as much information as possible relating to the problem, including print
screen(s) of the error.

@SMART

1 Solution Summary

This manual is designed to guide Lenders through the use of the Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery
Technology (SMART) System.

1.1 Features

The Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery Technology (SMART) System is comprised of individual
modules designed to assist the user in searching for specific loan information and performing related
functions. The modules currently available include the following:

Loan Module: Query and review loan information at a detailed level, add new loan records to
the system, and edit existing loan information.

Servicing Module: Assign mortgage servicing templates to individual loans, track the status of
each servicing template, and generate the corresponding servicing forms and letters.
Bankruptcy Module: Maintain, track, and edit bankruptcy information for individual loan
records.

Foreclosure Module: Manage loan records in the foreclosure process. Module provides a
timeline of the required foreclosure steps and tracks the scheduled foreclosure activity vs. the
completed foreclosure activity.

Mortgage Release Module: Initiate the loan release process for satisfied loans, track the release
status, and generate the corresponding release forms and letters.

Cash Management Module: Track and manage incoming payments from Pay.Gov, submit
disbursement checks, search for transactions and review the TROR and Trial Balance reports.
Customer Service Module: Create, view, and manage tickets. Create and edit call logs and ticket
actions.

Maintenance Module: Manage user account, reset user passwords, and update ticket round
robin.

The user is required to change their password every 30 days. The system maintains a password history,

If the user logs into SMART after their password is expired between 30 days and 90 days from their last
password change, they will be redirected to change their password. If the user has not logged on for 90
days, their account will be disabled. In order to reactivate their account, they will need to contact the
Help Desk. For information on how to contact the Help Desk, see Section 14: Getting Help.

multiple property inspection addresses, then the multiple Ticket Records tied to that Ticket Skey will no
longer display in the My Tickets Dashboard.

File Rec’d Date The File Received Date of a loan

EHLP Project # EHLP Project Number

Keyword Searches any word within the Search Results data table

4.2 Accessing Detailed Loan Information

Opening a Loan Record from the search results will navigate the user to the Loan Record page. The Loan
Record page consists of multiple tabs that provide detailed Loan information.

Step1: Click [LOAN] from the top Navigation menu. Select [SEARCH] from the dropdown.

Step 2: In the Loan Search Screen, select the Loan Program from the Loan Program drop down.

Step 3: Click [START SEARCH]. 50 records will display in the Search Results Dashboard.

Step 4: From the Search Results Dashboard, click on either the Loan Skey, FHA Case #, and Loan #
to open the loan.

Figure 28: Loan Record (example)

To minimize the loan record, click on the black arrow (+) located left of the Loan Record page title. To
maximize, re-click on the black arrow.

To minimize the Borrower & Property Information and Additional Loan Information, click on the white
arrow (Ez) located left of the of the Borrower & Property information box or the white arrow located left
of the Additional Loan Information. To maximize, re-click on the white arrow.

On each Loan Record page, the selection of tabs displayed is dynamic and varies depending on the Loan
program of the selected loan. The colors of the tabs show at a glance whether data exists in the tab or

not.

Note: Loans that are Closed are all Read Only.

9 Using the Cash Management Module

Within the Cash Management Module, there are two types of transactions: SMART and Pay.Gov.
SMART tickets are created using the SMART application. Pay.Gov transactions are payments that are
made on Pay.Gov and submitted via a validated submission forum to SMART. The © icon will appear
before or after the Pay.Gov Ticket Number anywhere a transaction appears (such as the Transactions
Tab within the Loan Module, Trial Balance - USSGL Account, and the Transaction Search Screen).

Data is refreshed on a nightly basis; however, if users need to refresh the data for today’s transactions,
they can do so from Cash Management. The Cash Management screens will display Transactions as of
the last data refresh.

@ Trial Balance

Figure 188: Data Refresh

Cc Last Data Refresh 12/04/2019 03-51-03 PM EST

Figure 189: Last Data Refresh

From any non-Pay.Gov screen under the Cash Management header, users will see a gold button below
the Help Desk button. By clicking it once, users can see the last time transaction data was refreshed. By
clicking it once more, users will refresh the data. Allow 1-2 minutes for the page to load.

10 Using the Customer Service Module

Within the Customer Service Module, there are two types of tickets: SMART and CRM. SMART tickets
are created using the SMART application. CRM (Customer Relationship Management), tickets are
created in a separate program used to track customer service tickets. CRM tickets are then imported
into SMART. The @ icon will appear before or after the CRM Ticket Number anywhere a Ticket appears
(such as My Tickets, All Inboxes, Ticket Search Screen, and within the Customer Service Module Ticket
Information Screen).

Additionally, there are two types of tickets: sys tickets and non-sys tickets. If a Loan No. exists for a
ticket, then that system is sys. If a Loan No. exists for a ticket, then that system is non-sys.

13.2 Solutions to Common Problems

Problems with SMART fall into three categories: internet issues, browser issues, and SMART issues.
Please follow the steps below to resolve each issue.

13.2.1 Internet and Browser Issues

The Primary characteristic of this issue is a delay when loading a page. At the conclusion of this long
delay, a message may display indicating there is a problem with internet access. Alternatively, pages
may seem to load but appear blank. If a page has not loaded or displayed after 30 seconds, please
follow the steps below.

Note: Not all steps have to be completed; start with Step 1 and keep working until the issue is resolved.
Once the issue is resolved, skip all remaining steps and return to your training session.

Step1: Refresh the page using the browser’s [REFRESH] button.

Step 2: _ If the issue still exists, close all browser windows, wait 10 seconds, then open a new
browser window and return to SMART.

SMART USER MANUAL | HUD.CC | VERSION 1.43.0 | JUNE 2, 2020 | 102

Step 3:

Step 4:

@SMART

Check your internet connectivity — do other sites display without issue? If so, proceed to
Step 2. Otherwise, the issue may be that the browser is unable to connect to the internet.
Check all connections and try again. If the problem persists, contact your network
administrator or your Internet Service Provider.

Send email to he!pdesk@hudnsc.org. Include your email address, your contact
information, and a description of what happened leading up to and following the issue.

13.2.2 SMART Issues

SMART issues may be errors which display on-screen or situations where data may not be saved
properly. If you experience either of these problems, please contact Support via email.

Step 1:
Step 2:

Step 3:

Use [PRTSC] on the keyboard to capture an image of the screen.

Compose a new email message and paste ([CTRL+V} on the keyboard) the screen image
into the message. Be sure to include your Username, your contact information, a
description of what module or page you were viewing, and what you were doing (or trying
to do) at the time the error occurred.

Send the email to helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

13.3 Getting More Help

If you are experiencing technical difficulties, please contact the SMART support team via email at
helpdesk@hudnsc.org. For general questions and/or class availability concerns, please contact the
SMART administration team via email at helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

When emailing, pleases include as much information as possible relating to the problem, including print
screen(s) of the error.

@SMART

1 Solution Summary

This manual is designed to guide Lenders through the use of the Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery
Technology (SMART) System.

1.1 Features

The Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery Technology (SMART) System is comprised of individual
modules designed to assist the user in searching for specific loan information and performing related
functions. The modules currently available include the following:

Loan Module: Query and review loan information at a detailed level, add new loan records to
the system, and edit existing loan information.

Servicing Module: Assign mortgage servicing templates to individual loans, track the status of
each servicing template, and generate the corresponding servicing forms and letters.
Bankruptcy Module: Maintain, track, and edit bankruptcy information for individual loan
records.

Foreclosure Module: Manage loan records in the foreclosure process. Module provides a
timeline of the required foreclosure steps and tracks the scheduled foreclosure activity vs. the
completed foreclosure activity.

Mortgage Release Module: Initiate the loan release process for satisfied loans, track the release
status, and generate the corresponding release forms and letters.

Cash Management Module: Track and manage incoming payments from Pay.Gov, submit
disbursement checks, search for transactions and review the TROR and Trial Balance reports.
Customer Service Module: Create, view, and manage tickets. Create and edit call logs and ticket
actions.

Maintenance Module: Manage user account, reset user passwords, and update ticket round
robin.

2.4.1. My Dashboard

The default page you come to after you have logged into SMART is the [My DASHBOARD] page. Under the
tab [My DASHBOARD] you have one option: My Loans.

2.4.2 Loan

The [LOAN] tab directs the user to the Loan Module in SMART. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.3 Servicing

The [SERVICING] tab directs the user to the Servicing Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.4 Bankruptcy

The [BANKRUPTCY] tab directs the user to the Bankruptcy Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.5 Foreclosure
The [FORECLOSURE] tab directs the user to the Foreclosure Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.6 Mortgage Release
The [MORTGAGE RELEASE] tab directs the user to the Mortgage Release Module. Here you have two
options: Mortgage Search and Check Search.

2.4.7. Cash Management
Under [CASH MANAGEMENT] you have four options: Trial Balance, TROR Report, Transaction Search, and
SPS.

2.4.8 Customer Service
The [CUSTOMER SERVICE] tab directs the user to the Customer Service Module. Here you have one option:
Ticket Search.

2.4.9 User Information and Roles

Select your user name to view and update your personal identification and contact information. You
may also change your password and security questions. From the [ROLE] drop-down menu, select the
role in which to view the SMART System.

the Change Password functionality on the My Account page. Follow the steps below to change your

The user is required to change their password every 30 days. The system maintains a password history,
so that 24 passwords cannot be reused.

If the user logs into SMART after their password is expired between 30 days and 90 days from their last
password change, they will be redirected to change their password. If the user has not logged on for 90
days, their account will be disabled. In order to reactivate their account, they will need to contact the
Help Desk. For information on how to contact the Help Desk, see Section 14: Getting Help.

Note: Each data table throughout the SMART system can generate reports in Excel, PDF or Print. The
Excel file is downloaded to your computer. Both PDF and Print opens in a new tab. You can also use the
search bar on any column to filter the data table results.

To open a Loan Record, click on the Loan Skey, FHA Case #, or Loan #.

If you have never pinned a loan to the My Loans tab of My Dashboard, then you will only see the Top 20
Most Recent Loans. If you have pinned a loan to the My Loans tab, then you will see all the loans you
have pinned and the Top 20 Most Recent Loans.

3.1.1 Pin Loan to My Loans Dashboard
Step 1: Identify a loan you would like to pin to the My Loans Dashboard.
Step 2: Once you have identified a loan you would like to pin, open that loan record.
Step 3: — Click [PIN TO DASHBOARD] button located in the top right corner of that loan record.

Once you have pinned a loan it will display on the My Loans Dashboard. If the loan has multiple

property inspection addresses, then the multiple Loan Records tied to that Loan Skey will display in the
My Loans Dashboard.

Search Field Definition

FHA Case # FHA Case number for each loan

Loan Skey SMART system identification number unique to each loan

Loan # HUD identification number for each loan.

Last 4 Digits of SSN The last four digits of the Borrower’s Social Security Number
Close Box # Physical location of stored files

Note Text Searches any word within the content of notes within the Notes tab of the Loan Record
Current Servicer Servicer/Lender associated with the FHA Case

Exception Type Type of Exception filed in the Exceptions tab

Result Headers Search criteria columns to be displayed in the Search Results table
Loan Program Type of program associated with the loan

Label Printed Indicator of whether or not a hard copy file has been generated for the loan
Loan Status Current high-level status of the Loan (Open or Closed)

Loan State Detailed Status of the loan

Payment Plan Type of Payment Plan associated with the loan

Note Type Type of note within the Notes tab of the Loan Record

Borrower Name Name of the Borrower

Property Address Address of the loan property

Property City City wherein the loan property is located

Property State State wherein the loan property is located

Property Zip Code Zip Code wherein the loan property is located

Note Created By SMART User who created Notes in the Notes tab

Claim Servicer Servicer/Lender associated with a Claim

Loan Create Date Date that a loan was entered into the SMART system

Loan Close Date Date that a loan was closed

File Rec’d Date The File Received Date of a loan

EHLP Project # EHLP Project Number

Keyword Searches any word within the Search Results data table

Note Create Date Date that the Note in the Notes tab was created

Payee/Holder of Record Servicer/Lender assigned as a Holder of Record

From the Search Results page, you can generate three different reports. The table below describes the
capabilities of the buttons located on the top left of the Search Results table. These options are also
available on all other Search Results pages within SMART.

Export to Excel Exports the data from the table into an excel spreadsheet.
Export to PDF Exports the data from the table into a .pdf file.
Print Displays the data from the table into a printable page.

returns back, the search criteria previously used will still show in the Search Screen Fields.

4.2 Accessing Detailed Loan Information

Opening a Loan Record from the search results will navigate the user to the Loan Record page. The Loan
Record page consists of multiple tabs that provide detailed Loan information.

Step1: Click [LOAN] from the top Navigation menu. Select [SEARCH] from the dropdown.

Step 2: In the Loan Search Screen, select the Loan Program from the Loan Program drop down.

Step 3: Click [START SEARCH]. 50 records will display in the Search Results Dashboard.

Step 4: From the Search Results Dashboard, click on either the Loan Skey, FHA Case #, and Loan #
to open the loan.

Figure 24: Loan Record (example)

To minimize the loan record, click on the black arrow (+) located left of the Loan Record page title. To
maximize, re-click on the black arrow.

To minimize the Borrower & Property Information and Additional Loan Information, click on the white
arrow (Ez) located left of the of the Borrower & Property information box or the white arrow located left
of the Additional Loan Information. To maximize, re-click on the white arrow.

On each Loan Record page, the selection of tabs displayed is dynamic and varies depending on the Loan
program of the selected loan. The colors of the tabs show at a glance whether data exists in the tab or

not.

Note: Loans that are Closed are all Read Only.

9 Using the Cash Management Module

Within the Cash Management Module, there are two types of transactions: SMART and Pay.Gov.
SMART tickets are created using the SMART application. Pay.Gov transactions are payments that are
made on Pay.Gov and submitted via a validated submission forum to SMART. The © icon will appear
before or after the Pay.Gov Ticket Number anywhere a transaction appears (such as the Transactions
Tab within the Loan Module, Trial Balance - USSGL Account, and the Transaction Search Screen).

Data is refreshed on a nightly basis; however, if users need to refresh the data for today’s transactions,
they can do so from Cash Management. The Cash Management screens will display Transactions as of
the last data refresh.

@ Trial Balance

Start Month 111201 >| End Month: 1/2 + | Display Type: snmary .
Summary of Account Chi

Figure 162: Data Refresh

Cc Last Data Refresh 12/04/2019 03-51-03 PM EST

Figure 163: Last Data Refresh

From any non-Pay.Gov screen under the Cash Management header, users will see a gold button below
the Help Desk button. By clicking it once, users can see the last time transaction data was refreshed. By
clicking it once more, users will refresh the data. Allow 1-2 minutes for the page to load.

10 Using the Customer Service Module

Within the Customer Service Module, there are two types of tickets: SMART and CRM. SMART tickets
are created using the SMART application. CRM (Customer Relationship Management), tickets are
created in a separate program used to track customer service tickets. CRM tickets are then imported
into SMART. The @ icon will appear before or after the CRM Ticket Number anywhere a Ticket appears
(such as My Tickets, All Inboxes, Ticket Search Screen, and within the Customer Service Module Ticket
Information Screen).

Additionally, there are two types of tickets: sys tickets and non-sys tickets. If a Loan No. exists for a
ticket, then that system is sys. If a Loan No. exists for a ticket, then that system is non-sys.

10.1 Ticket Search

Customer Service Tickets can be retrieved through various combinations of the search criteria available
on the Ticket Search Screen.

12.2 Solutions to Common Problems

Problems with SMART fall into three categories: internet issues, browser issues, and SMART issues.
Please follow the steps below to resolve each issue.

12.2.1 Internet and Browser Issues

The Primary characteristic of this issue is a delay when loading a page. At the conclusion of this long
delay, a message may display indicating there is a problem with internet access. Alternatively, pages
may seem to load but appear blank. If a page has not loaded or displayed after 30 seconds, please
follow the steps below.

Note: Not all steps have to be completed; start with Step 1 and keep working until the issue is resolved.
Once the issue is resolved, skip all remaining steps and return to your training session.

Step1: Refresh the page using the browser’s [REFRESH] button.

Step 2: If the issue still exists, close all browser windows, wait 10 seconds, then open a new
browser window and return to SMART.

SMART USER MANUAL | FHARC.READONLY | VERSION 1.43.0 | JUNE 2, 2020 | 83

Step 3:

Step 4:

@SMART

Check your internet connectivity — do other sites display without issue? If so, proceed to
Step 2. Otherwise, the issue may be that the browser is unable to connect to the internet.
Check all connections and try again. If the problem persists, contact your network
administrator or your Internet Service Provider.

Send email to he!pdesk@hudnsc.org. Include your email address, your contact
information, and a description of what happened leading up to and following the issue.

12.2.2. SMART Issues

SMART issues may be errors which display on-screen or situations where data may not be saved
properly. If you experience either of these problems, please contact Support via email.

Step 1:
Step 2:

Step 3:

Use [PRTSC] on the keyboard to capture an image of the screen.

Compose a new email message and paste ([CTRL+V} on the keyboard) the screen image
into the message. Be sure to include your Username, your contact information, a
description of what module or page you were viewing, and what you were doing (or trying
to do) at the time the error occurred.

Send the email to helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

12.3 Getting More Help

If you are experiencing technical difficulties, please contact the SMART support team via email at
helpdesk@hudnsc.org. For general questions and/or class availability concerns, please contact the
SMART administration team via email at helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

When emailing, pleases include as much information as possible relating to the problem, including print
screen(s) of the error.

@SMART

1 Solution Summary

This manual is designed to guide Lenders through the use of the Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery
Technology (SMART) System.

1.1 Features

The Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery Technology (SMART) System is comprised of individual
modules designed to assist the user in searching for specific loan information and performing related
functions. The modules currently available include the following:

Loan Module: Query and review loan information at a detailed level, add new loan records to
the system, and edit existing loan information.

Servicing Module: Assign mortgage servicing templates to individual loans, track the status of
each servicing template, and generate the corresponding servicing forms and letters.
Bankruptcy Module: Maintain, track, and edit bankruptcy information for individual loan
records.

Foreclosure Module: Manage loan records in the foreclosure process. Module provides a
timeline of the required foreclosure steps and tracks the scheduled foreclosure activity vs. the
completed foreclosure activity.

Mortgage Release Module: Initiate the loan release process for satisfied loans, track the release
status, and generate the corresponding release forms and letters.

Cash Management Module: Track and manage incoming payments from Pay.Gov, submit
disbursement checks, search for transactions and review the TROR and Trial Balance reports.
Customer Service Module: Create, view, and manage tickets. Create and edit call logs and ticket
actions.

Maintenance Module: Manage user account, reset user passwords, and update ticket round
robin.

2 Getting Started

2.1 Software Version
To access the SMART web application, open your web browser and go to: https://smart.hudnsc.org.

2.2 Solution Requirements
Users must have the following to use the SMART System:
e Screen Resolution 1920x1080 optimal
e =Internet Connection
e Web Browser (IE, Chrome, Firefox)
e Avalid user name, email address, and password
e Adobe Acrobat Reader or other .pdf reader (recommended)

Users may not use the following to access the SMART System:
e Mobile device with a screen size of 760px or less

As a web-based application, SMART is accessed through a web browser, and is not “installed” onto any
user’s computer.

2.3 Logging On
Once your SMART user profile has been created and approved, you may begin using the site. To Login,
follow the steps outlined below.

Step1: Toaccess the SMART web application, open your web browser and go to

https://smart.hudnsc.org.

2.4.1. My Dashboard

The default page you come to after you have logged into SMART is the [My DASHBOARD] page. Under the
tab [My DASHBOARD] you have one option: My Loans.

2.4.2 Loan

The [LOAN] tab directs the user to the Loan Module in SMART. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.3 Servicing

The [SERVICING] tab directs the user to the Servicing Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.4 Bankruptcy

The [BANKRUPTCY] tab directs the user to the Bankruptcy Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.5 Foreclosure
The [FORECLOSURE] tab directs the user to the Foreclosure Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.6 Mortgage Release
The [MORTGAGE RELEASE] tab directs the user to the Mortgage Release Module. Here you have two
options: Mortgage Search and Check Search.

2.4.7. Cash Management

Under [CASH MANAGEMENT] you have seven options: Trial Balance, TROR Report, Transaction Search, SPS,
Pay.Gov Dashboard, Pay.Gov Queue, and Review Failed CSV.

2.4.8 Reports

Under [REPoRTS] you have four options: Customer Service, Director Reports, Servicing/Release Reports,
and Accounting Reports.

2.4.9 User Information and Roles

Select your user name to view and update your personal identification and contact information. You
may also change your password and security questions. From the [ROLE] drop-down menu, select the
role in which to view the SMART System.

The user is required to change their password every 30 days. The system maintains a password history,

If the user logs into SMART after their password is expired between 30 days and 90 days from their last
password change, they will be redirected to change their password. If the user has not logged on for 90
days, their account will be disabled. In order to reactivate their account, they will need to contact the
Help Desk. For information on how to contact the Help Desk, see Section 14: Getting Help.

Search Field Definition

FHA Case # FHA Case number for each loan

Loan Skey SMART system identification number unique to each loan

Loan # HUD identification number for each loan.

Last 4 Digits of SSN The last four digits of the Borrower’s Social Security Number
Close Box # Physical location of stored files

Note Text Searches any word within the content of notes within the Notes tab of the Loan Record
Current Servicer Servicer/Lender associated with the FHA Case

Exception Type Type of Exception filed in the Exceptions tab

Result Headers Search criteria columns to be displayed in the Search Results table
Loan Program Type of program associated with the loan

Label Printed Indicator of whether or not a hard copy file has been generated for the loan
Loan Status Current high-level status of the Loan (Open or Closed)

Loan State Detailed Status of the loan

Payment Plan Type of Payment Plan associated with the loan

Note Type Type of note within the Notes tab of the Loan Record

Borrower Name Name of the Borrower

Property Address Address of the loan property

Property City City wherein the loan property is located

Property State State wherein the loan property is located

Property Zip Code Zip Code wherein the loan property is located

Note Created By SMART User who created Notes in the Notes tab

Claim Servicer Servicer/Lender associated with a Claim

Loan Create Date Date that a loan was entered into the SMART system

Loan Close Date Date that a loan was closed

File Rec’d Date The File Received Date of a loan

EHLP Project # EHLP Project Number

Keyword Searches any word within the Search Results data table

Note Create Date Date that the Note in the Notes tab was created

Payee/Holder of Record Servicer/Lender assigned as a Holder of Record

4.2 Accessing Detailed Loan Information

Opening a Loan Record from the search results will navigate the user to the Loan Record page. The Loan
Record page consists of multiple tabs that provide detailed Loan information.

Step1: Click [LOAN] from the top Navigation menu. Select [SEARCH] from the dropdown.

Step 2: In the Loan Search Screen, select the Loan Program from the Loan Program drop down.

Step 3: Click [START SEARCH]. 50 records will display in the Search Results Dashboard.

Step 4: From the Search Results Dashboard, click on either the Loan Skey, FHA Case #, and Loan #
to open the loan.

Figure 24: Loan Record (example)

To minimize the loan record, click on the black arrow (+) located left of the Loan Record page title. To
maximize, re-click on the black arrow.

To minimize the Borrower & Property Information and Additional Loan Information, click on the white
arrow (Ez) located left of the of the Borrower & Property information box or the white arrow located left
of the Additional Loan Information. To maximize, re-click on the white arrow.

On each Loan Record page, the selection of tabs displayed is dynamic and varies depending on the Loan
program of the selected loan. The colors of the tabs show at a glance whether data exists in the tab or

not.

Note: Loans that are Closed are all Read Only.

9 Using the Cash Management Module

Within the Cash Management Module, there are two types of transactions: SMART and Pay.Gov.
SMART tickets are created using the SMART application. Pay.Gov transactions are payments that are
made on Pay.Gov and submitted via a validated submission forum to SMART. The © icon will appear
before or after the Pay.Gov Ticket Number anywhere a transaction appears (such as the Transactions
Tab within the Loan Module, Trial Balance - USSGL Account, and the Transaction Search Screen).

Data is refreshed on a nightly basis; however, if users need to refresh the data for today’s transactions,
they can do so from Cash Management. The Cash Management screens will display Transactions as of
the last data refresh.

@ Trial Balance

Start Month 111201 >| End Month: 1/2 + | Display Type: snmary .
Summary of Account Chi

Figure 184: Data Refresh

Cc Last Data Refresh 12/04/2019 03-51-03 PM EST

Figure 185: Last Data Refresh

From any non-Pay.Gov screen under the Cash Management header, users will see a gold button below
the Help Desk button. By clicking it once, users can see the last time transaction data was refreshed. By
clicking it once more, users will refresh the data. Allow 1-2 minutes for the page to load.

select [PAY.GOv DASHBOARD] from the dropdown. The Pay.Gov Dashboard summarizes all settled

is in the validation process. The Dashboard is organized by the daily .xml file that is retrieved from
Pay.Gov by the SMART system. Each file name contains a link that will open a detailed dashboard with
all transactions retrieved from that day.

12.2 Solutions to Common Problems

Problems with SMART fall into three categories: internet issues, browser issues, and SMART issues.
Please follow the steps below to resolve each issue.

12.2.1 Internet and Browser Issues

The Primary characteristic of this issue is a delay when loading a page. At the conclusion of this long
delay, a message may display indicating there is a problem with internet access. Alternatively, pages
may seem to load but appear blank. If a page has not loaded or displayed after 30 seconds, please
follow the steps below.

Note: Not all steps have to be completed; start with Step 1 and keep working until the issue is resolved.
Once the issue is resolved, skip all remaining steps and return to your training session.

Step1: Refresh the page using the browser’s [REFRESH] button.

Step 2: _ If the issue still exists, close all browser windows, wait 10 seconds, then open a new
browser window and return to SMART.

SMART USER MANUAL | HUD.ACCOUNTING | VERSION 1.43.0 | JUNE 2, 2020 | 94

Step 3:

Step 4:

@SMART

Check your internet connectivity — do other sites display without issue? If so, proceed to
Step 2. Otherwise, the issue may be that the browser is unable to connect to the internet.
Check all connections and try again. If the problem persists, contact your network
administrator or your Internet Service Provider.

Send email to he!pdesk@hudnsc.org. Include your email address, your contact
information, and a description of what happened leading up to and following the issue.

12.2.2. SMART Issues

SMART issues may be errors which display on-screen or situations where data may not be saved
properly. If you experience either of these problems, please contact Support via email.

Step 1:
Step 2:

Step 3:

Use [PRTSC] on the keyboard to capture an image of the screen.

Compose a new email message and paste ([CTRL+V} on the keyboard) the screen image
into the message. Be sure to include your Username, your contact information, a
description of what module or page you were viewing, and what you were doing (or trying
to do) at the time the error occurred.

Send the email to helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

12.3 Getting More Help

If you are experiencing technical difficulties, please contact the SMART support team via email at
helpdesk@hudnsc.org. For general questions and/or class availability concerns, please contact the
SMART administration team via email at helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

When emailing, pleases include as much information as possible relating to the problem, including print
screen(s) of the error.

@SMART

1 Solution Summary

This manual is designed to guide Lenders through the use of the Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery
Technology (SMART) System.

1.1 Features

The Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery Technology (SMART) System is comprised of individual
modules designed to assist the user in searching for specific loan information and performing related
functions. The modules currently available include the following:

Loan Module: Query and review loan information at a detailed level, add new loan records to
the system, and edit existing loan information.

Servicing Module: Assign mortgage servicing templates to individual loans, track the status of
each servicing template, and generate the corresponding servicing forms and letters.
Bankruptcy Module: Maintain, track, and edit bankruptcy information for individual loan
records.

Foreclosure Module: Manage loan records in the foreclosure process. Module provides a
timeline of the required foreclosure steps and tracks the scheduled foreclosure activity vs. the
completed foreclosure activity.

Mortgage Release Module: Initiate the loan release process for satisfied loans, track the release
status, and generate the corresponding release forms and letters.

Customer Service Module: Create, view, and manage tickets. Create and edit call logs and ticket
actions.

Maintenance Module: Manage user account, reset user passwords, and update ticket round
robin.

The [LOAN] tab directs the user to the Loan Module in SMART. Here you have one option: Search.

The [SERVICING] tab directs the user to the Servicing Module. Here you have one option: Search.

The [CUSTOMER SERVICE] tab directs the user to the Customer Service Module. Here you have two

Reports.

Select your user name to view and update your personal identification and contact information. You
may also change your password and security questions.

2.4.7 Role

From the [ROLE] drop-down menu, select the role in which to view the SMART System.

2.4.8 Maintenance

The [MAINTENANCE] tab directs the user to the Maintenance Module. Here you have one option: Ticket
Round Robin.

Step 3: Click [START SEARCH]. Twenty records will display in the Search Results Dashboard.

Step 4: From the Search Results Dashboard, click on either the Loan Skey, FHA Case #, and Loan #
to open the loan.

Mortgage/Loss Mitigation/Housing Counseling Information Box.

10.2 Solutions to Common Problems

Problems with SMART fall into three categories: internet issues, browser issues, and SMART issues.
Please follow the steps below to resolve each issue.

10.2.1 Internet and Browser Issues

The Primary characteristic of this issue is a delay when loading a page. At the conclusion of this long
delay, a message may display indicating there is a problem with internet access. Alternatively, pages
may seem to load but appear blank. If a page has not loaded or displayed after 30 seconds, please
follow the steps below.

Note: Not all steps have to be completed; start with Step 1 and keep working until the issue is resolved.
Once the issue is resolved, skip all remaining steps and return to your training session.

Step 1: Refresh the page using the browser’s [REFRESH] button.

Step 2: _ If the issue still exists, close all browser windows, wait 10 seconds, then open a new
browser window and return to SMART.

USER MANUAL | HUD.CSTEAMLEADHECM | JUNE 10, 2019 | 84

Step 3:

Step 4:

@SMART

Check your internet connectivity — do other sites display without issue? If so, proceed to
Step 2. Otherwise, the issue may be that the browser is unable to connect to the internet.
Check all connections and try again. If the problem persists, contact your network
administrator or your Internet Service Provider.

Send email to helpdesk@hudnsc.org. Include your email address, your contact
information, and a description of what happened leading up to and following the issue.

10.2.2 SMART Issues

SMART issues may be errors which display on-screen or situations where data may not be saved
properly. If you experience either of these problems, please contact Support via email.

Step 1:
Step 2:

Step 3:

Use [PRTSC] on the keyboard to capture an image of the screen.

Compose a new email message and paste ([CTRL+V} on the keyboard) the screen image
into the message. Be sure to include your Username, your contact information, a
description of what module or page you were viewing, and what you were doing (or trying
to do) at the time the error occurred.

Send the email to helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

10.3 Getting More Help

If you are experiencing technical difficulties, please contact the SMART support team via email at
helpdesk@hudnsc.org. For general questions and/or class availability concerns, please contact the
SMART administration team via email at helodesk@hudnsc.org.

When emailing, pleases include as much information as possible relating to the problem, including print
screen(s) of the error.

@SMART

1 Solution Summary

This manual is designed to guide Lenders through the use of the Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery
Technology (SMART) System.

1.1 Features

The Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery Technology (SMART) System is comprised of individual
modules designed to assist the user in searching for specific loan information and performing related
functions. The modules currently available include the following:

Loan Module: Query and review loan information at a detailed level, add new loan records to
the system, and edit existing loan information.

Servicing Module: Assign mortgage servicing templates to individual loans, track the status of
each servicing template, and generate the corresponding servicing forms and letters.
Bankruptcy Module: Maintain, track, and edit bankruptcy information for individual loan
records.

Foreclosure Module: Manage loan records in the foreclosure process. Module provides a
timeline of the required foreclosure steps and tracks the scheduled foreclosure activity vs. the
completed foreclosure activity.

Mortgage Release Module: Initiate the loan release process for satisfied loans, track the release
status, and generate the corresponding release forms and letters.

Cash Management Module: Track and manage incoming payments from Pay.Gov, submit
disbursement checks, search for transactions and review the TROR and Trial Balance reports.
Customer Service Module: Create, view, and manage tickets. Create and edit call logs and ticket
actions.

Maintenance Module: Manage user account, reset user passwords, and update ticket round
robin.

To minimize the Borrower & Property Information and Additional Loan Information, click on the white
arrow (Ez) located left of the of the Borrower & Property information box or the white arrow located left
of the Additional Loan Information. To maximize, re-click on the white arrow.

On each Loan Record page, the selection of tabs displayed is dynamic and varies depending on the Loan
program of the selected loan. The colors of the tabs show at a glance whether data exists in the tab or

not.

Note: Loans that are Closed are all Read Only.

Click [SERVICING] from the top Navigation menu. Select [SEARCH] from the dropdown.
Select the search criteria from the displayed search fields in the Servicing Search Screen.

Search Field Definition

FHA Case # FHA Case number for each loan

Loan Skey SMART system identification number unique to each loan
Loan # HUD identification number for each loan.

Lender Name Lender associated with the FHA Case

Close Box # Physical location of stored files.

Last 4 digits of SSN The last four digits of the Borrower's Social Security Number
Note Type Type of note within the Notes tab of the Loan Record

Result Headers

Search criteria columns to be displayed in the Search Results table

Loan Program

Type of program associated with the loan

Loan Status

Current high-level status of the Loan (Open or Closed)

Loan State

Detailed Status of the loan

Payment Plan

Type of Payment Plan associated with the loan

Servicing Status

Indicator that the servicing type is completed or is still pending completion by the user.

Servicing Step

Servicing activity step associated with the servicing activity timeline

Note Text Searches any word within the content of notes within the Notes tab of the Loan Record
Borrower Name Name of the Borrower

Property Address Address of the loan property

Property State State wherein the loan property is located

Servicing Step Status

Indicator the step is completed or is still pending completion by the user

Servicing Type

Type of servicing activity assigned to a loan in the form of a predefined template of servicing
activity steps

Note Created By

SMART User who created Notes in the Notes tab

Loan Create Date

Date that a loan was entered into the SMART system

Loan Close Date

Date that a loan was closed

Orig Lend Amt From

Original principal amount of the loan in dollars (numerals only)

Scheduled Date

The date that a servicing activity step is scheduled to be completed by the user.

Servicing Completed Date

The date that a servicing activity step is actually completed by the user

Keyword

Keyword search.

Note Create Date

Date that the Note in the Notes tab was created

6 Using the Customer Service Module

Within the Customer Service Module, there are two types of tickets: SMART and CRM. SMART tickets
are created using the SMART application. CRM (Customer Relationship Management), tickets are
created in a separate program used to track customer service tickets. CRM tickets are then imported
into SMART. The @ icon will appear before or after the CRM Ticket Number anywhere a Ticket appears
(such as My Tickets, All Inboxes, Ticket Search Screen, and within the Customer Service Module Ticket
Information Screen).

Additionally, there are two types of tickets: sys tickets and non-sys tickets. If a Loan No. exists for a
ticket, then that system is sys. If a Loan No. exists for a ticket, then that system is non-sys.

6.1 Ticket Search

Customer Service Tickets can be retrieved through various combinations of the search criteria available
on the Ticket Search Screen.

8.2 Solutions to Common Problems

Problems with SMART fall into three categories: internet issues, browser issues, and SMART issues.
Please follow the steps below to resolve each issue.

8.2.1 Internet and Browser Issues

The Primary characteristic of this issue is a delay when loading a page. At the conclusion of this long
delay, a message may display indicating there is a problem with internet access. Alternatively, pages
may seem to load but appear blank. If a page has not loaded or displayed after 30 seconds, please
follow the steps below.

Note: Not all steps have to be completed; start with Step 1 and keep working until the issue is resolved.
Once the issue is resolved, skip all remaining steps and return to your training session.

Step1: Refresh the page using the browser’s [REFRESH] button.

Step 2: If the issue still exists, close all browser windows, wait 10 seconds, then open a new
browser window and return to SMART.

SMART USER MANUAL | HUD.CSHECM | VERSION 1.43.0 | JUNE 2, 2020 | 76

@SMART

Step 3: Check your internet connectivity — do other sites display without issue? If so, proceed to
Step 2. Otherwise, the issue may be that the browser is unable to connect to the internet.
Check all connections and try again. If the problem persists, contact your network
administrator or your Internet Service Provider.

Step 4: Send email to helpdesk@hudnsc.org. Include your email address, your contact
information, and a description of what happened leading up to and following the issue.

8.2.2 SMART Issues

SMART issues may be errors which display on-screen or situations where data may not be saved
properly. If you experience either of these problems, please contact Support via email.

Step 1: Use [PRTSC] on the keyboard to capture an image of the screen.

Step 2: Compose a new email message and paste ([CTRL+V} on the keyboard) the screen image
into the message. Be sure to include your Username, your contact information, a
description of what module or page you were viewing, and what you were doing (or trying
to do) at the time the error occurred.

Step 3: Send the email to helopdesk@hudnsc.org.

8.3 Getting More Help

If you are experiencing technical difficulties, please contact the SMART support team via email at
helpdesk@hudnsc.org. For general questions and/or class availability concerns, please contact the
SMART administration team via email at helpdesk@hudnsc.org.

When emailing, pleases include as much information as possible relating to the problem, including print
screen(s) of the error.

@SMART

1 Solution Summary

This manual is designed to guide Lenders through the use of the Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery
Technology (SMART) System.

1.1 Features

The Single-Family Mortgage Asset Recovery Technology (SMART) System is comprised of individual
modules designed to assist the user in searching for specific loan information and performing related
functions. The modules currently available include the following:

Loan Module: Query and review loan information at a detailed level, add new loan records to
the system, and edit existing loan information.

Servicing Module: Assign mortgage servicing templates to individual loans, track the status of
each servicing template, and generate the corresponding servicing forms and letters.
Bankruptcy Module: Maintain, track, and edit bankruptcy information for individual loan
records.

Foreclosure Module: Manage loan records in the foreclosure process. Module provides a
timeline of the required foreclosure steps and tracks the scheduled foreclosure activity vs. the
completed foreclosure activity.

Mortgage Release Module: Initiate the loan release process for satisfied loans, track the release
status, and generate the corresponding release forms and letters.

Customer Service Module: Create, view, and manage tickets. Create and edit call logs and ticket
actions.

Maintenance Module: Manage user account, reset user passwords, and update ticket round
robin.

The default page you come to after you have logged into SMART is the [My DASHBOARD] page. Under the
tab [My DASHBOARD] you have four options: My Tickets, Supervisor Inbox, HUD Inbox, and Action List.

2.4.2. Loan

The [LOAN] tab directs the user to the Loan Module in SMART. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.3 Servicing

The [SERVICING] tab directs the user to the Servicing Module. Here you have one option: Search.

2.4.4 Customer Service
The [CUSTOMER SERVICE] tab directs the user to the Customer Service Module. Here you have two
options: Ticket Search and Create New Ticket.

2.4.5 Reports

Under [REPORTS] you have three options: Customer Service, Director Reports, and Servicing/Release
Reports.

2.4.6 User Information

Select your user name to view and update your personal identification and contact information. You
may also change your password and security questions.

2.4.7 Role

From the [ROLE] drop-down menu, select the role in which to view the SMART System.

2.4.8 Maintenance

The [MAINTENANCE] tab directs the user to the Maintenance Module. Here you have one option: Ticket
Round Robin.

Help Desk. For information on how to contact the Help Desk, see Section 14: Getting Help.

program of the selected loan. The colors of the tabs show at a glance whether data exists in the tab or

not.

Figure 162: Servicing Search Screen

Click [SERVICING] from the top Navigation menu. Select [SEARCH] from the dropdown.
Select the search criteria from the displayed search fields in the Servicing Search Screen.

Search Field Definition

FHA Case # FHA Case number for each loan

Loan Skey SMART system identification number unique to each loan
Loan # HUD identification number for each loan.

Lender Name Lender associated with the FHA Case

Close Box # Physical location of stored files.

Last 4 digits of SSN The last four digits of the Borrower’s Social Security Number
Note Type Type of note within the Notes tab of the Loan Record

Result Headers

Search criteria columns to be displayed in the Search Results table

Loan Program

Type of program associated with the loan

Loan Status

Current high-level status of the Loan (Open or Closed)

Loan State

Detailed Status of the loan

Payment Plan

Type of Payment Plan associated with the loan

Servicing Status

Indicator that the servicing type is completed or is still pending completion by the user.

Servicing Step

Servicing activity step associated with the servicing activity timeline

Note Text Searches any word within the content of notes within the Notes tab of the Loan Record
Borrower Name Name of the Borrower

Property Address Address of the loan property

Property State State wherein the loan property is located

Servicing Step Status

Indicator the step is completed or is still pending completion by the user
